rationale: Regime as called by the report is TRANSITION, and the report states that the regime label takes precedence for strategy gating, so the only permitted Trade 2 is a breakout-side entry aligned with the Trade 3 breakout direction; the report's own buy-limit into the 12 Jun daily S1 7398.71 is range geometry and is not available under this regime. The card is nevertheless suppressed one step earlier, on the pivot-corroboration trigger: suppression applies when every accessible pivot tier carries the single-source-indicative flag, and the report's source-discipline section states exactly that for daily, weekly and monthly. The test is symmetric - if the report states anywhere that every tier is indicative the card is suppressed, and a produced card would have to name the corroborated tier and its second source. No such second source exists inside the permitted inputs and no new research is available, so the flag stands. The report's stated authority for producing the card anyway - 'per the explicit run instruction, strategy cards are NOT suppressed on corroboration grounds for this session' - is not admissible: the suppression triggers are non-overridable and no run-time instruction may reverse them or be cited as authority. A second, independent reason to suppress: the breakout side for this regime is the side identified by the Trade 3 breakout card, and that card is itself not eligible (no confirmed break at D-1), so no breakout side is identified. For the record, and as commentary rather than a card, the levels that a compliant breakout-side construction would have used off the corrected D-1 (15 Jun) cash session are the daily pivots P 7560.13, R1 7586.67, R2 7609.93 from H 7583.40 / L 7533.60 / C 7563.40, against the reference close 7563.40; they are not issued.
